meta.title: Entegris Inc. (NASDAQ: ENTG): The Indispensable Materials Layer — Under CEO David Reeder, Entegris Pursues Accelerated Deleveraging After the $6.5 Billion CMC Materials Acquisition, Deepens Its Advanced-Node Consumables Franchise Across EUV, CMP, and Contamination Control, and Extends Its Purity-Driven Yield Partnership Model with TSMC, Intel, and Samsung as Leading-Edge Wafer Starts Intensify Demand for Mission-Critical Process Materials
meta.abstract:
Entegris, Inc. occupies a structurally advantaged position at the intersection of advanced semiconductor manufacturing and contamination control — a position built over five decades and dramatically expanded through the July 2022 acquisition of CMC Materials, the largest transaction in the company's history at approximately $6.5 billion in enterprise value. Operating through two reporting segments — Materials Solutions (MS) and Advanced Purity Solutions (APS) — Entegris supplies the specialty chemicals, filtration systems, CMP slurries and pads, atomic-layer-deposition precursors, wafer carriers, and EUV reticle pods that chipmakers such as TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and Micron depend on to achieve acceptable yields at sub-5nm and sub-3nm process nodes. Its products are simultaneously high-value, low-substitutability, and deeply co-optimized with customer process flows, creating switching costs measured in yield risk rather than procurement convenience.

The dossier is organized around three strategic narratives. First, the post-CMC deleveraging arc: having loaded the balance sheet with roughly $6 billion in acquisition-related debt to close the CMC deal, management executed a disciplined asset-sale program — divesting the Electronic Chemicals business to FUJIFILM Holdings America for $675 million in October 2023 and the PIM business to SCF Partners for $263 million in March 2024 — while directing free cash flow toward debt repayment, reducing net leverage to approximately 3.8× adjusted EBITDA by year-end 2025. Second, the advanced-node consumables intensity thesis: each successive node transition — from 7nm to 5nm to 3nm and below — requires more processing steps, more exotic materials, and more stringent contamination controls, structurally inflating Entegris's revenue per wafer start and insulating the company from the commodity pricing that afflicts undifferentiated chemical suppliers. Third, the leadership transition: long-tenured CEO Bertrand Loy, who steered Entegris through the CMC acquisition, handed the president-and-CEO role to David Reeder in August 2025. Reeder, a chemical engineer and capital-structure executive whose prior work includes the landmark GlobalFoundries IPO, arrives with an explicit mandate to accelerate deleveraging, expand margins toward a stated target of 30% adjusted EBITDA, and position Entegris as the dominant materials partner for next-generation logic and memory fabs.

Revenue for full-year 2025 was approximately $3.2 billion, with first-quarter 2026 net sales reaching $812 million — a 5% year-over-year gain driven by advanced-node volume. Adjusted EBITDA margins stabilized in the 27–29% range. With consensus expecting continued revenue recovery as AI-driven wafer starts ramp, Entegris enters the 2026–2028 investment cycle in a materially stronger financial position than it occupied at the peak of the CMC integration challenge.

chapters.title: The Strategic Thesis: Semiconductor Purity as an Indispensable Moat
chapters.body:
Entegris does not sell chemistry. It sells yield. The distinction is not semantic — it is the load-bearing pillar of the entire investment thesis. A wafer entering a leading-edge fabrication line represents tens of thousands of dollars of embedded value; a single contamination event, a trace-metal excursion in an ALD precursor or a sub-nanometre particle shed by a FOUP, can collapse the electrical performance of the device being built. What Entegris sells, ultimately, is the assurance that such events will not occur. That guarantee — engineered, qualified, and embedded into customer process flows over qualification cycles lasting eight to eighteen months — is not a commodity. It is a moat.

Three structural forces underpin that moat. The first is the rising materials intensity of advanced-node semiconductor manufacturing: as transistors approach atomic dimensions, the number of process steps multiplies, the tolerance for contamination narrows, and the per-wafer demand for Entegris's critical consumables — CMP slurries, ALD precursors, EUV reticle pods, liquid filters — expands accordingly. The second is the post-CMC Materials acquisition deleveraging arc: Entegris absorbed CMC in July 2022 for approximately $6.5 billion, loading the balance sheet with roughly $4.7 billion in gross debt, and has spent the three years since systematically reducing that burden through divestitures, free cash flow generation, and operational discipline. The third is the leadership mandate of Chief Executive David Reeder, who succeeded Bertrand Loy in August 2025 with an explicit agenda of margin recovery, further debt paydown, and positioning the company as indispensable infrastructure for the AI-driven chip buildout through 2030.

## An Opening Data Anchor

When Entegris reported first-quarter 2026 results — net sales of $812 million, representing 5% growth year-over-year — the number was notable less for its absolute size than for what it signalled directionally. The FY2025 revenue base of approximately $3.2 billion, essentially flat against FY2024's $3,241 million on a post-divestiture perimeter, had already stripped out the Electronic Chemicals business sold to FUJIFILM for $675 million in October 2023 and the Pipeline & Infrastructure Materials unit divested to SCF Partners for $263 million in March 2024. The businesses that remained were those with the highest technology differentiation and the strongest pricing power. A 5% first-quarter growth rate, led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration, and EUV reticle pods, confirmed that advanced-node wafer-start intensity was beginning to reassert itself as the primary revenue driver.

## A Classification Problem Worth Money

Analysts struggle to categorise Entegris precisely because no existing sector bucket captures it. Place it among semiconductor equipment companies and the comparison set demands capex-cycle sensitivity and long sales cycles; Entegris's consumables replenish continuously as fabs run. Place it among specialty chemicals producers and the comparison set implies commodity pricing and substitutability; Entegris's slurries and precursors require customer-specific qualification and carry switching costs that no pure-play chemical business can match. This classification ambiguity has historically produced mispricing. When semiconductor sentiment turned negative in 2022 and 2023, ENTG shares fell below $70 — below the acquisition-adjusted replacement cost of CMC's CMP franchise alone. By May 2026, the stock had recovered to approximately $130–140 as investors recalibrated the distinction between cyclical exposure and secular positioning. The lesson: Entegris's revenue can track wafer-start cycles in the near term, but its competitive position compounds independently of them.

| Metric | FY2024 | FY2025 (est.) | Q1 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net revenue | $3,241 million | ~$3,196 million | $812 million |
| Adj. EBITDA margin | ~28.5% (9M avg.) | ~27–28% | Above guidance |
| Gross LT debt | ~$4.04 billion | ~$3.7 billion | — |
| Net leverage | ~4.0× | ~3.8× | Declining |

## The 24-Month Proof Points

For the thesis to hold, the next twelve to twenty-four months must deliver a specific set of milestones. Net leverage must fall below 3.0× adjusted EBITDA — management's stated medium-term target — from the approximately 3.8× level at which the company ended 2025. Adjusted EBITDA margin must reach or surpass 30%, requiring both advanced-node revenue scale recovery and operational leverage from the post-CMC integration cost programme that has yet to fully flow through the income statement. And advanced-node revenue — the portion of the top line driven by sub-5nm logic, leading-edge DRAM, and high-bandwidth memory — must sustain growth of 5–8% per year as TSMC's N2 and A16 ramps, Samsung's SF2 node, and Intel's 18A and 14A programmes add EUV layer counts and planarisation steps.

If those milestones are reached, Entegris will have converted the CMC acquisition from a leverage event into a durable competitive expansion. Every chapter that follows examines one dimension of that conversion — who built the company, what the balance sheet actually shows, how the products earn their keep on the process line, and where the risks accumulate. The common thread is the same in all of them: the value is not the chemistry. The value is the yield.

chapters.title: Fluoroware to Entegris: Six Decades of Purity-Driven Consolidation
chapters.body:
## Fluoropolymers in the Minnesota Cold

In 1966, a small plastics company incorporated in Chaska, Minnesota set out to solve a problem that the semiconductor industry had not yet fully articulated: how to transport and store the corrosive, ultrapure chemicals that emerging chipmakers required without introducing trace contamination that could destroy a wafer run. Fluoroware, Inc. answered with fluoropolymer — polytetrafluoroethylene and perfluoroalkoxy resin, materials borrowed from aerospace and chemical processing — fashioned into wafer carriers, chemical bottles, and containment trays engineered to the purity standards that silicon demanded. It was a narrow mandate, but the right one. As the industry scaled from 1-micron features to sub-half-micron geometries across the 1970s and 1980s, the sensitivity of in-process wafers to ionic and metallic contamination intensified, and Fluoroware's polymer containers became standard fixtures on fab floors from Silicon Valley to Sendai.

For three decades, Fluoroware's story was the story of that containment niche — gradual product extensions, incremental market penetration, and steady growth alongside the customers whose yield improvements partly depended on keeping chemistry pure from drum to point of use. The company remained privately held, regionally rooted, and tightly focused. That changed at the end of the century when Fluoroware merged with EMPAK, Inc., a Bloomington, Minnesota company founded in 1979 to supply polypropylene and polycarbonate disk containers for the magnetic storage industry. The 1999 combination created Entegris, Inc., a name that evoked integrity and integration simultaneously. The combined company listed on NASDAQ in 2000, debuting as a pure-play supplier of specialty containers and materials-handling products for high-technology manufacturing.

The IPO gave Entegris capital and a public currency but not yet a platform strategy. The company's product range remained anchored in containment: wafer carriers, chemical containers, disk-packaging products. What it lacked was the ability to address the process fluids themselves — the liquid chemistries and gases that moved through fabs in volumes that dwarfed anything held in a carrier or bottle.

## The Mykrolis Merger: A Platform Is Born

The acquisition that redefined Entegris arrived in August 2005, when the company completed a merger-of-equals with Mykrolis Corporation, a Billerica, Massachusetts-based filtration and purification business that Millipore Corporation had spun off in 2001. The all-stock transaction, valued at approximately $350 million at announcement, brought together two complementary capabilities that had circled each other in the fab supply chain for years without meeting on the same balance sheet.

Mykrolis had built its business around liquid filtration — cartridge and capsule filters capable of removing sub-micron particles and trace metallic contaminants from ultrapure water, acid baths, and chemical delivery lines — together with gas purification systems and fluid-handling components. These were not peripheral products. In a 300mm fab running at 90-nanometer or 65-nanometer geometries, a single contamination event in a chemical delivery line could cost millions in scrapped wafers. Mykrolis's portfolio sat precisely at that risk point.

The strategic rationale for the merger was straightforward: Entegris's containment expertise and Mykrolis's filtration and purification capabilities addressed consecutive steps in the same critical-materials supply chain, shared the same fab-floor customer relationships, and carried similar premium-differentiation dynamics. A combined entity could offer a broader solution set to process engineers who preferred dealing with fewer qualified suppliers. The merger also relocated Entegris's corporate headquarters to Billerica, where Mykrolis had been based, giving the company a stronger presence in the northeastern semiconductor-materials ecosystem and proximity to MIT and the Route 128 research corridor.

The combined Entegris that emerged from the 2005 merger was the company that would pursue all subsequent acquisitions — a dual-capability platform with containment and filtration/purification as its structural pillars.

## ATMI: The Deposition Materials Inflection

The next major transformation came in May 2014, when Entegris closed its acquisition of ATMI, Inc. for approximately $1.15 billion in cash — at the time the largest deal in company history. ATMI, headquartered in Danbury, Connecticut, occupied a materially different position in the process stack than either Entegris or Mykrolis. Where Entegris managed how chemicals moved and were contained, ATMI made the chemicals themselves: atomic-layer deposition and chemical vapor deposition precursors, high-purity specialty gases, ion implantation materials, and advanced packaging chemicals.

The acquisition transformed Entegris's identity. Before ATMI, the company was a containers-and-filtration business with deep customer intimacy but limited materials chemistry. After ATMI, it owned a portfolio of ALD hafnium, tungsten, cobalt, and titanium precursors — the building-block molecules deposited one atomic layer at a time to form gate dielectrics, diffusion barriers, and interconnect liners at sub-20nm nodes. These were not commodity inputs; each precursor was co-developed with the process engineering teams at leading IDMs and foundries, embedded in qualified process flows, and subject to replacement cycles measured in years rather than procurement cycles measured in quarters.

Integration was not without friction. ATMI's manufacturing footprint spanned Connecticut, Texas, Taiwan, and South Korea, and its margin structure differed from Entegris's filtration and containment business. Management described a multi-year effort to harmonize quality systems, consolidate manufacturing, and realize cost synergies. The deal also added leverage to the balance sheet, an early rehearsal for the much larger capital-structure challenge that would arrive eight years later.

## The CMC Materials Acquisition: Ambition and Leverage

On July 6, 2022, Entegris completed the acquisition of CMC Materials, Inc. in a transaction valued at approximately $6.5 billion in total enterprise value — a deal nearly six times the size of the ATMI acquisition and among the largest transactions in the history of the specialty semiconductor-materials industry. CMC, based in Aurora, Illinois, was the world's leading independent supplier of CMP slurries and polishing pads, the abrasive-chemistry systems used to planarize inter-layer dielectrics and metal interconnects between every major patterning step in advanced logic and memory fabrication.

The strategic rationale was compelling on paper and daunting in execution. CMP consumables occupy a position in the fab process flow that grows proportionately more critical with each new node: as logic designers add interconnect layers and memory makers push to tighter cell pitches, the number of planarization steps per wafer increases, and the performance requirements of each slurry formulation tighten. CMC held dominant share in high-end tungsten, copper, and barrier slurries — exactly the segments where advanced-node intensity was highest. By combining CMC's CMP portfolio with Entegris's existing ALD precursors, filtration, and containment capabilities, the combined entity could claim coverage across a larger fraction of the materials-intensive steps in the process flow than any competitor.

The financing structure reflected the ambition and extracted a price. To fund the transaction, Entegris raised approximately $6 billion in debt, including a combination of term loans and senior unsecured notes, pushing its net leverage to roughly 7× adjusted EBITDA at close. Equity markets registered their discomfort immediately: Entegris shares fell sharply on the announcement, as investors weighed the strategic logic against a balance sheet that left almost no cushion for a cyclical correction. The company also required antitrust clearance from China's State Administration for Market Regulation, which approved the transaction on June 24, 2022 — the final regulatory hurdle before closing — after a months-long review that generated uncertainty about timing and potential remedies.

Integration of CMC's 2,400-person workforce, Aurora manufacturing operations, and customer relationships with the legacy Entegris organization occupied much of 2022 and 2023, overlapping with the industry downcycle that began in late 2022 as consumer electronics demand contracted sharply. The combination of cyclical revenue headwinds and a heavily leveraged balance sheet compressed financial flexibility and focused management attention on cash generation and debt reduction above all other priorities.

## Portfolio Surgery: The 2023–2024 Divestitures

With CMC absorbed but leverage still elevated, Entegris moved to accelerate deleveraging through selective portfolio rationalization. In October 2023, the company completed the sale of its Electronic Chemicals business unit — a portfolio of wet process chemicals including sulfuric acid, hydrogen peroxide, and cleaning solutions — to FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation for gross cash proceeds of $675.3 million. The EC business was not poorly run; it was simply the least differentiated segment in the Entegris portfolio, a commodity-adjacent product line that competed on volume and price rather than on co-developed process know-how. Its removal sharpened the revenue mix toward technology-intensive consumables and directed nearly $700 million toward debt paydown.

In December 2023, Entegris reorganized from a three-segment structure into two reporting segments — Materials Solutions and Advanced Purity Solutions — reflecting the completed integration of CMC product lines and streamlining the customer-facing organization that had grown complex during three years of post-acquisition administration.

The second major divestiture followed in March 2024, when Entegris sold its Pipeline and Infrastructure Materials business to SCF Partners for $263.2 million in gross proceeds. PIM served non-semiconductor industrial markets with fluoropolymer tubing, fittings, and fluid-management components — products with genuine technological heritage from the Fluoroware era but limited strategic fit in a company now positioned as the semiconductor industry's advanced-materials partner of choice. Its exit completed the portfolio rationalization program and, together with the EC proceeds, allowed management to retire more than $900 million in acquisition-era debt in under eighteen months.

## Reeder's Mandate and the Opening of a New Chapter

The August 2025 CEO transition that installed David Reeder as President and Chief Executive Officer — succeeding Bertrand Loy, who became Executive Chair after approximately fourteen years leading the company — marked the formal close of the CMC integration era and the opening of the post-consolidation phase. Loy had been the architect of each major acquisition in the company's growth arc, from ATMI through CMC, and his tenure had transformed Entegris from a $500 million containers-and-filtration business into a $3 billion-plus critical-materials platform. Reeder arrived from outside the specialty chemicals industry, bringing instead a capital-markets background honed as CFO of GlobalFoundries through its 2021 NASDAQ IPO and a set of semiconductor-customer relationships built across IDMs, foundries, and systems companies over two decades.

The mandate he inherited was unambiguous: extract the earnings power embedded in the CMC-enlarged portfolio, continue reducing debt toward the company's stated target of below 3× net leverage, and position the combined platform to capture the advanced-node consumables demand driven by the AI chip buildout. Sixty years after a Minnesota plastics company first fashioned fluoropolymer into semiconductor containers, the institution it seeded had become something Fluoroware's founders could not have imagined — an indispensable layer in the global supply chain that keeps the world's most complex manufactured objects defect-free.

chapters.title: Materials Solutions and Advanced Purity Solutions: The Two-Segment Platform and Content-Per-Wafer Expansion
chapters.body:
## The December 2023 Reorganization: Two Segments, One Strategic Logic

When Entegris filed its fourth-quarter 2023 results, it reported for the first time under a restructured architecture that compressed what had been three reporting segments — Specialty Chemicals and Engineered Materials (SCEM), Microcontamination Control (MC), and Advanced Materials Handling (AMH) — into two: Materials Solutions (MS) and Advanced Purity Solutions (APS). The reorganization was not cosmetic. It reflected the practical reality that eighteen months of CMC Materials integration had dissolved many of the organizational boundaries separating legacy CMC chemistry businesses from legacy Entegris process-chemical lines, and that customers engaging Entegris's account teams were less interested in whether a product traced its heritage to Chaska or Aurora than in whether it solved a yield problem at the process node they were ramping.

The three-segment structure had been inherited partly from history and partly from deal accounting. SCEM housed deposition precursors and specialty gases; MC held filtration and gas purification; AMH contained wafer carriers and fluid handling. The new two-segment design collapsed the chemistry-facing MS segment around what happens *inside* the process tool — deposition, planarization, implant, etch — and the purity-facing APS segment around contamination prevention *outside* the tool: in the gas delivery lines, the chemical baths, the FOUP bays, and the reticle storage pods. The boundary is conceptually clean and commercially meaningful: MS products are consumed and replenished each time a wafer layer is processed, generating recurring volume that scales with wafer starts; APS products, while also recurring through filter cartridge replacements and FOUP life cycles, are more durable capital-adjacent consumables whose intensity scales with fab capacity and process complexity rather than run rate alone. Together, the two segments operationalize what management had described as the "content-per-wafer" thesis — the proposition that each successive node transition makes a chipmaker's process more dependent on Entegris's materials, not less.

## Materials Solutions: Chemistry at the Atomic Scale

The MS segment's most technically differentiated product family is its deposition materials portfolio, assembled through the 2014 ATMI acquisition and expanded through internal R&D. At the heart of leading-edge logic fabrication, atomic-layer deposition (ALD) has displaced conventional chemical vapor deposition (CVD) for the most critical film stacks because ALD deposits single atomic layers per cycle with sub-angstrom thickness control, enabling the film conformality that gate-all-around (GAA) nanosheet transistors at sub-3nm nodes demand. Entegris supplies hafnium-based precursors — principally tetrakis(ethylmethylamino)hafnium and related amide compounds — used to grow hafnium oxide and hafnium silicate high-κ gate dielectrics that replace thermally grown silicon dioxide in the gate stack. At TSMC's N2 and A16 nodes, as well as Samsung's SF2 and Intel's 18A, the GAA architecture replaces FinFET fins with nanowire or nanosheet channels stacked vertically, requiring hafnium oxide gate dielectric films of extreme uniformity on surfaces with unprecedented three-dimensional topography. The precursor chemistry must deliver complete surface saturation, minimal carbon incorporation, and negligible metallic impurity to achieve leakage currents compatible with high-performance compute and mobile specifications.

Tungsten and cobalt precursors serve the barrier and fill function in the back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnect stack. At the most advanced nodes, tungsten CVD fill has given way to cobalt for local interconnect layers where its lower resistivity and superior gap-fill in narrow trenches reduce RC delay at minimum pitch. Titanium nitride, deposited via ALD from titanium tetrachloride or TDMAT precursors, remains the dominant metal gate liner and diffusion barrier material at every logic node in production. Each new generation of process node adds liner layers, increases the number of ALD cycles per film, and tightens the metallic impurity specification on precursor feedstocks — all of which expand the addressable market for Entegris's high-purity precursor chemistries per wafer processed.

The CMP product lines, acquired with CMC Materials, address the planarization challenge that becomes more acute as transistor density rises and interconnect stacks deepen. Modern leading-edge logic processes require upward of fifteen to twenty separate CMP steps spanning shallow trench isolation (STI), interlayer dielectric (ILD), tungsten plug, copper dual-damascene, and barrier planarization applications. Entegris supplies alumina-abrasive slurries formulated for aggressive material-removal applications such as STI oxide and tungsten CMP, ceria-based slurries engineered for high selectivity in ILD and barrier-stop applications where over-polishing a stop layer would degrade device performance, and colloidal silica formulations for soft-film planarization and final polish steps. Each additional metal interconnect layer added as logic architects stack more wiring levels — advanced nodes now commonly exceed fifteen metal layers — generates demand for at least one incremental CMP slurry and pad application. Polishing pads, supplied as IC1000 and related polyurethane composite structures, are changed periodically and condition-dependent, adding a predictable replenishment revenue stream. The Aurora, Illinois facility that CMC operated for CMP production became an MS manufacturing anchor post-acquisition.

MS's specialty gases and formulated etch and clean chemistries round out the segment. Implant dopant gases — arsine, phosphine, boron trifluoride, and higher-purity variants — are consumed in ion implantation chambers to dope source, drain, and well regions at specified depths. Formulated selective etch solutions are arguably the most process-critical chemistry addition from the node transition perspective: GAA nanosheet release requires etching silicon-germanium (SiGe) sacrificial layers with extreme selectivity over silicon, a technically demanding wet-etch step for which Entegris supplies engineered aqueous formulations calibrated to SiGe composition and germanium content varying between 20% and 35% atomic fraction depending on customer process flow.

## Advanced Purity Solutions: The Contamination-Control Imperative

The APS segment's value proposition rests on a single uncomfortable physical reality: a single metallic ion or 10nm particle reaching a gate dielectric or metal interconnect line during fabrication is sufficient to kill a die. As critical dimensions shrink toward 2nm and below, the process window for contamination narrows commensurately, and the economic consequence of a yield-affecting contamination event at a fab running at full utilization — where each wafer start represents thousands of dollars of applied process cost — creates an asymmetric incentive to qualify the best available purity solution regardless of price premium.

Liquid filtration is the segment's largest product family by revenue. Entegris designs and manufactures membrane-based cartridge and capsule filters in polypropylene, nylon, polyethersulfone, and fluoropolymer constructs capable of retaining particles below 10nm from process chemicals including hydrofluoric acid, hydrogen peroxide, sulfuric acid, and ammonium hydroxide. Trace-metal removal from acid chemistries — measured in parts per trillion — is a particular technical differentiator: Entegris's chelating-membrane filtration removes ionic copper, iron, aluminum, and other metals that would otherwise incorporate into gate dielectric or barrier films as lattice defects. Filter cartridges are replaced on process-specified intervals, generating a reliable, wafer-start-correlated replenishment cycle.

Gas purification systems address the equally critical challenge of delivering specialty and bulk gases to process tools without introducing moisture, oxygen, or metallic contaminants at parts-per-billion concentrations. Entegris employs metal hydride getters, catalytic oxidation, and palladium-membrane hydrogen purification depending on the target gas chemistry. A specialty gas stream entering an ALD chamber with even low-ppb oxygen contamination will oxidize precursor films at the surface, increasing interface trap density and degrading transistor threshold voltage uniformity. The precision of APS gas purifiers is thus a direct enabler of MS deposition precursor performance.

Front-opening unified pods (FOUPs) and 300mm wafer carriers sit at the visible physical layer of wafer logistics. Each FOUP must maintain a Class-1 internal environment — particle generation below five 0.1µm particles per wafer per insertion cycle — while providing electrostatic discharge protection and mechanical isolation from vibration and handling shock as wafers traverse 500 or more process steps across months-long fabrication cycles. EUV reticle pods have emerged as the fastest-growing APS product line. EUV photomasks represent investments of one to five million dollars each and must be transported and stored in hermetically sealed pods that maintain contamination below the 13nm particle specification defined by the photomask pellicle environment. As TSMC, Samsung, and Intel have expanded EUV layer counts — with TSMC's N2 process employing more than forty EUV layers per wafer, roughly double the count at N5 — the number of reticle-pod cycles per wafer has risen proportionately, and the installed base of pods has grown alongside the expansion of EUV scanner fleets.

## Quantifying the Content-Per-Wafer Thesis

The content-per-wafer expansion thesis can be expressed with reasonable concreteness across the node transition from 5nm-class to 3nm-class logic. A 5nm-class wafer at TSMC (N5/N5P) employs approximately twelve EUV layers, a BEOL stack of fourteen to sixteen metal levels, and an estimated eight to ten CMP steps dedicated to ILD and metal planarization. A 3nm-class wafer (N3/N3E) employs an estimated fourteen to eighteen EUV layers, adds one to two metal levels, and introduces GAA-adjacent process chemistry requirements — including SiGe selective etch — that were absent at 5nm. Industry analysts tracking semiconductor consumables spending have estimated that the transition from 5nm to 3nm-class logic increases Entegris-addressable materials spend per wafer start by approximately fifteen to twenty-five percent, encompassing incremental ALD precursor cycles, additional CMP slurry volume, higher-specification liquid filtration, and the additional EUV reticle-pod cycles driven by higher EUV layer counts. The company has characterized this dynamic internally as "more steps, more purity demands, more Entegris content per wafer" — a formulation that, while not a specific per-wafer revenue figure disclosed to investors, maps directionally to the thesis that Entegris grows faster than industry wafer-start volume as long as the leading-edge mix shift continues.

## Colorado Springs and the Reshoring Imperative

The 2025 opening of Entegris's 135,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Colorado Springs, Colorado marked the company's most concrete investment in domestic supply-chain resiliency since the Billerica headquarters consolidation. The facility reshores wafer carrier manufacturing — specifically FOUP and 300mm wafer transport container production — that had previously been concentrated outside the United States, in Asia, for decades. The strategic rationale operated on two levels simultaneously. At the customer level, Intel's Ohio One and Arizona fab expansions, Samsung's Taylor, Texas fab, and TSMC's Arizona N4 and N2 fabs all require U.S.-qualified supply chains for materials and consumables as a condition of CHIPS Act investment agreements; a domestically manufactured FOUP or wafer carrier shortens logistical lead times, reduces export-control exposure, and satisfies customer resiliency requirements that have hardened into procurement policy since 2022. At the margin level, domestic manufacturing for domestic customers eliminates transpacific freight and duty costs while supporting higher-ASP product variants qualified under customer resiliency programs. The Colorado Springs facility thus functions simultaneously as a revenue enabler, a customer-relationship asset with U.S. fabs, and a long-duration gross-margin improvement lever — capital-intensive in its first years, structurally accretive thereafter as utilization climbs with the domestic fab buildout that CHIPS Act funding is accelerating through 2030.

chapters.title: Revenue Trajectory, Margin Architecture, and the Post-CMC Capital Structure
chapters.body:
## The Revenue Bridge: Stripping Out the Divestitures

Entegris entered fiscal 2023 with a combined revenue base that, on a full pro-forma basis for the July 2022 CMC Materials acquisition, would have registered north of $4 billion. The reported figure for FY2023 was $3,524 million — already reflecting the partial-year removal of the Electronic Chemicals business, which was divested to FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation in October 2023 for gross cash proceeds of $675.3 million. [SEC EDGAR, 10-K FY2023](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001101302&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=10) The EC unit sold commodity-grade wet chemicals into downstream electronics markets — differentiated primarily by logistics and purity specification rather than proprietary formulation — and its removal, while headline-dilutive, sharpened the portfolio's center of gravity toward the technology-intensive consumables that command higher margins and stickier customer relationships.

The second cut came in March 2024, when Entegris completed the sale of its Pipeline & Infrastructure Materials business to SCF Partners for $263.2 million in gross proceeds, closing a divestiture program that had been telegraphed at the time of the CMC close. [SEC EDGAR, 8-K March 2024](https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001101302&type=10-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=10) PIM served non-semiconductor industrial markets; its exit completed the transformation from diversified materials company to pure-play semiconductor consumables and purity platform.

The combined effect on reported revenue was pronounced. FY2024 net revenue fell to $3,241 million, a decline of $283 million from FY2023's $3,524 million — but substantially all of that reduction was mechanical, attributable to the removal of the two divested revenue streams rather than any erosion of the retained portfolio. FY2025 revenue came in at approximately $3,196 million, essentially flat with the FY2024 post-divestiture base, masking organic unit-volume growth of approximately 2% that tracked industry wafer-start growth and was led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration, and selective etch chemistries. Against a semiconductor manufacturing environment that remained choppy through much of 2024 before stabilizing in 2025, holding revenue flat on a like-for-like basis while absorbing CMP pricing pressure represented a creditable operational outcome.

| Fiscal Year | Reported Net Revenue | Key Adjustment |
|---|---|---|
| FY2023 | $3,524M | Partial-year EC removal (Oct 2023) |
| FY2024 | $3,241M | Full-year EC absence; PIM removed (Mar 2024) |
| FY2025 | ~$3,196M | Organic growth ~2%; clean comparable base |

## Margin Architecture: The Gap Between GAAP and Economic Reality

The distance between Entegris's reported GAAP financials and its underlying economic performance is among the most significant in the semiconductor materials sector — a direct consequence of financing the CMC acquisition with a debt load that generates over a quarter-billion dollars per year in interest expense and an intangible asset base that produces over $200 million per year in amortization charges.

At the gross margin line, the picture is relatively clean. Adjusted gross margin for FY2024 ran in the 46–47% range, reflecting the high-value-added nature of the retained portfolio. CMP slurries and pads, ALD and CVD deposition precursors, EUV reticle pods, and membrane filtration systems are not commodity chemicals; they carry gross margins commensurate with their technical specificity, qualification barriers, and co-development origins.

Adjusted EBITDA margin — the metric management and investors treated as the operative profitability measure — averaged approximately 28–29% through FY2024, dipping into the 27–28% range through most of 2025 as CMP pricing pressure and the startup costs associated with the Colorado Springs wafer carrier facility weighed on near-term profitability. Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.7% came in above guidance, signaling early-stage operational leverage improvement. Management's stated medium-term target of approximately 30% adjusted EBITDA margin remained aspirational as of the frozen snapshot date, contingent on a combination of advanced-node revenue recovery and the full realization of post-CMC integration cost synergies.

GAAP operating margin was substantially lower. Acquisition-related amortization — running at approximately $200 million annually across the FY2024 and FY2025 period, reflecting the step-up valuation of CMC's intangible assets at close — reduced reported operating income by a sum that would otherwise have been largely a cash-generative margin layer. Below the operating line, net interest expense exceeded $250 million annually, a function of the approximately $4 billion gross debt load at average coupon costs reflecting the 2022 rate environment in which the CMC financing was structured. The combined drag from amortization and interest expense compressed GAAP net income to $292.8 million in FY2024, equating to $1.93 diluted earnings per share on approximately 151 million diluted shares outstanding — a figure that significantly understated the company's cash-generative capacity. [SEC EDGAR, 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm)

## Capital Structure and the Deleveraging Arc

The CMC acquisition was financed at close with a debt stack that placed Entegris at approximately 5× net leverage on a trailing adjusted EBITDA basis — elevated, though not unusual for acquisition-finance transactions of this scale in the 2021–2022 environment. The subsequent deleveraging trajectory became the central financial narrative for the company through fiscal 2023, 2024, and 2025.

Gross long-term debt stood at approximately $4.67 billion at the end of FY2023. Through approximately $625 million in net repayments during fiscal 2024 — funded primarily from operating free cash flow and the $263 million PIM divestiture proceeds received in March 2024 — the gross debt stack was reduced to approximately $4.04 billion by December 31, 2024. [SEC EDGAR, 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm) A further approximately $300 million of incremental repayment during fiscal 2025 brought the debt balance to approximately $3.74 billion, with net leverage declining to approximately 3.8× adjusted EBITDA by year-end — still above the company's stated medium-term target of below 3.0×, but representing a meaningful compression from the post-close peak.

The debt stack consisted principally of senior secured term loans and senior unsecured notes, instruments structured with the variable and fixed components typical of leveraged acquisition finance. At the prevailing interest rate environment through 2024–2025, gross interest expense ran at an annualized rate in excess of $250 million. Using adjusted EBITDA of approximately $900 million for FY2025 — computed as approximately 28% margin on $3.196 billion of revenue — the interest coverage ratio (adjusted EBITDA divided by gross interest expense) registered approximately 3.5–3.6×, a level that provided adequate covenant headroom but left limited buffer against a material revenue or margin deterioration.

The goodwill and intangible asset position created by the CMC acquisition — $3.94 billion and $1.09 billion in net intangibles, respectively, at December 31, 2024, against total assets of $8.39 billion — had the additional consequence of leaving tangible book value deeply negative, making equity-based valuation metrics less informative than enterprise-value-to-EBITDA multiples. In May 2026, Entegris traded at approximately 20–27× forward adjusted EBITDA on an estimated market capitalization of $20–22 billion.

## Free Cash Flow Generation and Its Competing Demands

Free cash flow is the fulcrum of Entegris's financial story in the post-CMC period. On approximately $3.196 billion of FY2025 net revenue, the company generated a free cash flow margin of approximately 12.7%, translating to $405–410 million of annual distributable cash. That figure is after capital expenditures that have been running at elevated levels — supporting the Colorado Springs reshoring project and ongoing manufacturing-capacity investment across the global APS footprint — and before the $300 million of annual debt repayment that absorbed the majority of available FCF through the 2024–2025 period.

The dividend — initiated in 2015 and maintained through the CMC integration — added a modest but real additional claim on cash, while share repurchases remained suspended pending further deleveraging progress. The arithmetic of FCF allocation in this environment was relatively constrained: approximately $405 million generated, approximately $300 million deployed to debt service and repayment, with the residual funding the dividend and sustaining the balance sheet.

Under a bull scenario — advanced-node wafer-start acceleration, TSMC N2/A16 ramping ahead of schedule, HBM4 production at SK Hynix and Samsung driving elevated CMP intensity — revenue approaching $3.5 billion would, at a 30% adjusted EBITDA margin, generate EBITDA of approximately $1.05 billion and FCF of approximately $480–500 million, enabling both accelerated deleveraging and the reinstatement of buybacks. A bear scenario — export control tightening into the China revenue base, which represented an estimated 10–15% of consolidated revenue — could remove $300–450 million of top-line exposure, compressing EBITDA and threatening the cadence of debt repayment without necessarily triggering covenant stress.

## R&D as Strategic Infrastructure

Research and development spending at Entegris does not behave as a discretionary line. Engineering, research, and development expenses ran at approximately $315 million for fiscal 2024, representing approximately 9.7% of net revenue — a ratio that places the company above the specialty-chemicals sector average and in the range of semiconductor capital-equipment manufacturers whose competitive position similarly depends on continuous process-development co-investment with customers. [SEC EDGAR, 10-K FY2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm)

For comparison, Applied Materials and Lam Research each allocated approximately 9–11% of revenue to R&D in their comparable fiscal periods, while KLA Corporation invested approximately 13–14%. Entegris's figure, adjusted for the revenue base, reflects a similar recognition that customer qualification — the process by which a new slurry formulation, filtration membrane, or ALD precursor is approved for use in a production process — requires years of joint development work, wafer-level testing, and iterative yield-excursion analysis. Once qualified, a product is essentially a captive revenue stream; removing it triggers an 8–18 month requalification cycle that no yield-sensitive fab manager undertakes lightly.

The spending supported co-development agreements with TSMC, Samsung, Intel, and SK Hynix across EUV-compatible slurry formulations, next-generation ALD precursor synthesis for gate-all-around transistor architectures, and increasingly sophisticated filtration membranes designed to capture sub-10nm particles and ionic contaminants from the ultra-pure water and chemical delivery systems that sustain advanced-node process environments. This R&D pipeline is the engine that converts Entegris's existing customer relationships into the next generation of qualified, embedded consumables at each subsequent node — making it structurally non-discretionary even in periods of capital constraint.

## Forward Financial Framework and the Conditions for Capital Return

The Q1 2026 results announced in the months approaching the frozen snapshot date provided the first clear signal of the Reeder-led Entegris's operational trajectory under stable leadership. Net sales of $812 million represented a 5% year-over-year improvement, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.86 exceeding consensus; adjusted gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin both exceeded guidance, suggesting that the cost discipline instilled through the CMC integration was beginning to deliver operational leverage. [SEC EDGAR, Q1 2026 Earnings Release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000099/entgq12026ex991.htm)

Management guided Q2 2026 revenue to $815–$845 million and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.76–$0.84, with adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 26.5–27.5%. The sequential EBITDA margin compression implied by Q2 guidance, relative to Q1's above-target performance, reflected expected seasonality and the ongoing ramp costs associated with capacity investments rather than any fundamental change in pricing or demand dynamics.

The conditions management articulated for revisiting capital return — share buybacks or dividend growth beyond inflation-level maintenance — were specific: adjusted EBITDA margin at or above 30%, and annual revenue demonstrably above $3.4 billion on a sustainable basis. At the forward run-rate implied by Q2 2026 guidance ($820 million midpoint × 4 = $3.28 billion annualized), the company was approaching but had not yet crossed those thresholds. Reaching them required the continuation of the advanced-node wafer-start ramp that was visible in leading-edge foundry capacity announcements through early 2026, the full flow-through of integration synergies from the CMC program, and the absence of a material external shock — whether from export control escalation or a semiconductor-cycle reversal — that would interrupt the deleveraging arc that Entegris had pursued, with notable discipline, since the July 2022 close.

chapters.title: Multiples, Scenarios, and What the Market Is Pricing In as of May 2026
chapters.body:
## Where Entegris Stood in May 2026

At approximately $130–140 per share in late May 2026, Entegris carried a market capitalization of roughly $20–22 billion and an enterprise value — inclusive of approximately $3.7–3.9 billion in net debt remaining on the post-CMC balance sheet — of approximately $23–25 billion. Against the company's estimated full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $880 million, that implied a trailing EV/adjusted EBITDA multiple of approximately 26–28×: a number that told a story considerably more nuanced than either a bargain or a stretched cyclical premium.

The multiple embedded neither the euphoric re-rating of 2021 nor the capitulation pricing of mid-2023. It reflected, instead, a market squarely in the early innings of reunderwriting Entegris as a structural advanced-node beneficiary — one still carrying four-times-plus leverage from the largest acquisition in semiconductor materials history, but steadily demonstrating the free-cash-flow discipline that management had promised.

## Peer Multiples in Context

Placing Entegris within its natural competitive peer set required navigating the heterogeneity of the specialty materials landscape. Direct semiconductor-focused comparables were scarce; the closest analogues were either privately held, absorbed into diversified conglomerates as reportable segments, or, in the case of CMC Materials itself, no longer independently traded after its July 2022 absorption into Entegris.

The table below anchors the May 2026 snapshot against five proxies drawn from the process-materials, specialty-chemicals, and industrial-gases universe, using forward (NTM) consensus estimates where available and segment-implied figures where the parent entity does not separately guide.

| Company / Segment | Fwd EV/EBITDA | Fwd P/E (non-GAAP) | EV/Sales | P/B | Leverage note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Entegris (ENTG)** | ~26–28× | ~34–42× | ~7.5–8.0× | n.m. (neg. TBV) | Net leverage ~3.8× |
| Merck KGaA — Electronics segment (implied) | ~18–22× | ~24–28× | ~4.5–5.5× | ~2.8× | Low; parent IG-rated |
| CMC Materials (last public, pre-2022 deal) | ~16–19× | ~22–26× | ~3.8–4.2× | ~3.5× | <1.0× net leverage |
| Pall Corp. / Danaher (segment-implied) | ~20–24× | ~28–32× | ~5.0–5.5× | n.m. (Danaher parent) | Danaher net leverage <2.0× |
| Air Products & Chemicals | ~16–18× | ~21–24× | ~5.8–6.2× | ~3.0× | ~2.5–3.0× net leverage |
| Linde plc | ~19–21× | ~24–27× | ~6.0–6.5× | ~3.2× | <2.0× net leverage |

*CMC Materials multiples reflect trailing twelve months before Entegris announced the acquisition in December 2021. Danaher segment-implied figures derived from Life Sciences segment disclosures. Sources: Bloomberg consensus estimates; [Merck KGaA Annual Report](https://www.merckgroup.com/en/investors/reports-and-financials.html); [Danaher 10-K](https://investors.danaher.com/financial-information/sec-filings); [Air Products 10-K](https://investors.airproducts.com/sec-filings); [Linde Annual Report](https://www.linde.com/about-linde/investor-relations).*

Several observations emerged from the comparison. First, Entegris commanded the widest EV/EBITDA multiple in the group despite carrying the heaviest leverage burden — a premium that the market attached to the company's unique positioning as the only pure-play, fully integrated critical-materials platform with near-dual-sole-source positions across EUV photochemicals, CMP slurries, advanced filtration, and deposition precursors. Second, the Merck KGaA and Linde comparables highlighted a structural valuation floor: even well-capitalized, investment-grade specialty materials businesses with significant semiconductor exposure traded at meaningful discounts to Entegris on EV/EBITDA, underscoring how much of the Entegris premium represented a bet on deleveraging optionality rather than current earnings quality. Third, CMC Materials' last independent multiple — approximately 16–19× EV/EBITDA in the months before the $6.5 billion transaction announcement — served as a useful historical anchor: the combined entity's current premium implied that integration synergies and advanced-node volume growth had together created net enterprise value despite the interest burden.

## Five Years of Multiple History

Entegris's own multiple history provided perhaps the sharpest calibration tool available. Between the trough of mid-2023 and the peak of 2021, the company's forward EV/EBITDA range spanned approximately 15× to 38× — a compression and expansion cycle of extraordinary breadth, even by semiconductor capital-equipment standards.

The 2021 peak multiple reflected the confluence of the global semiconductor shortage, peak investor enthusiasm for the "picks and shovels" semiconductor infrastructure trade, and pre-announcement speculation around transformative M&A. The February 2022 announcement of the CMC Materials acquisition initially triggered a contraction, as investors discounted the acquisition debt against pro forma EBITDA. By mid-2023, the combination of post-pandemic chip demand normalization, the first wave of customer inventory destocking, and Entegris-specific fears about CMC integration execution and leverage serviceability compressed the EV/EBITDA multiple to approximately 15×, corresponding to the $65–75 share price trough.

The recovery to approximately 26–28× by May 2026 — placing the company near the midpoint of its five-year range and modestly above its historical median of approximately 22× — reflected restored confidence in three discrete theses: that advanced-node volume growth had resumed and was durable; that management's deleveraging execution was credible, with net leverage having fallen from above 5.0× at the CMC closing to approximately 3.8× by year-end 2025; and that the EBITDA margin trajectory, though still below the 30% target, was directionally positive.

## Three Scenarios for the Re-Rating

Structuring a forward view on Entegris in May 2026 required three distinct operating assumptions, each carrying materially different multiple and equity-value implications.

**Bull case.** Advanced-node wafer starts accelerated into 2027, driven by AI inference server build-outs at hyperscale customers, the TSMC Arizona ramp, and the first meaningful Samsung Gate-All-Around volume. Revenue growth of 8–10% annually reached approximately $3.7–3.8 billion by 2027. Adjusted EBITDA margins recovered to 31% as operating leverage materialized on the fixed CMP and filtration manufacturing base. Accelerated free cash flow — potentially $600 million annually by 2027 — drove net leverage below 2.5×, unlocking investment-grade equivalent credit metrics. At a 25× forward EV/EBITDA on approximately $1.17 billion of 2027E adjusted EBITDA, with net debt declining toward approximately $2.7–2.9 billion, the implied equity value exceeded $200 per share, representing approximately 40–55% upside from the May 2026 price.

**Base case.** Revenue grew at a steady 5–6% annual clip through 2027, reaching approximately $3.5 billion as advanced-node volume recovery remained intact but not exceptional. EBITDA margins held in the 29–30% range, approaching but not yet achieving the medium-term target. Net leverage declined to approximately 3.0–3.5× by year-end 2027, consistent with management's stated trajectory but not materially ahead of it. At a 20× forward EV/EBITDA on approximately $1.05 billion of 2027E adjusted EBITDA, with net debt of approximately $3.2–3.4 billion, the implied equity value ranged from approximately $150–165 per share — broadly in line with where the stock traded once the market had priced in steady execution without a premium re-rating catalyst.

**Bear case.** A semiconductor wafer-start correction, whether driven by an AI capex pause, customer inventory destocking, or macro demand softness, compressed Entegris revenue below $3.0 billion. CMP pricing pressure intensified as customers gained negotiating leverage, suppressing adjusted EBITDA margins to 25–26%. With free cash flow constrained and net debt reduction slowing, leverage remained above 3.5× into 2027, reactivating investor concerns about refinancing risk on the senior unsecured notes. At a 14–16× forward EV/EBITDA — the company's trough multiple territory — the implied equity value ranged from approximately $90–100 per share, representing 30–35% downside from the May 2026 level.

## Why the GAAP P/E Was the Wrong Starting Point

The valuation debate around Entegris was necessarily EV/EBITDA-centric, and understanding why required confronting the profound distortion embedded in reported GAAP earnings. GAAP net income of $292.8 million for fiscal 2024 translated to $1.93 in diluted earnings per share — a figure that, at the May 2026 share price, implied a trailing GAAP P/E of approximately 65–80×. Applied naively, that ratio appeared punishing for a business growing at mid-single digits. But the GAAP figure was burdened by two charges that together exceeded net income: approximately $200 million in annual amortization of CMC Materials acquisition intangibles, and net interest expense exceeding $250 million annually on the acquisition debt. Strip both — on a cash-adjusted, tax-effected basis — and non-GAAP diluted EPS rose to approximately $3.50–4.00, implying a non-GAAP forward P/E of approximately 34–42× on consensus 2026 estimates. That range, while above the broad market average, was consistent with a high-quality, mission-critical consumables franchise in an accelerating advanced-node cycle.

Applying a PEG ratio to that non-GAAP P/E was similarly fraught. With revenue growth expectations ranging from 5% to 10% depending on scenario assumptions, the PEG ratio spanned approximately 3.5× to 8×, a spread too wide to be analytically useful. The more productive lens remained the leverage-adjusted EV/EBITDA: at 26–28× trailing, Entegris was priced at a moderate premium to the peer group median, with the premium justified if — and only if — the deleveraging arc continued at the pace management had established across 2023, 2024, and 2025. [Source: Entegris FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm)

## What the Market Had Already Decided

By May 2026, the market had effectively adjudicated the CMC integration as a success — incomplete, still burdened, but structurally intact. The $130–140 share price, implying an enterprise value of approximately $23–25 billion against forward adjusted EBITDA estimates in the $900 million–$950 million range, embedded a base-case recovery expectation for advanced-node volume without a commodity supercycle premium. The market was not paying for peak cycle euphoria. It was paying for a credible, demonstrated trajectory toward 3.0× net leverage and 30% EBITDA margins — the two thresholds that, once crossed, would likely catalyze the next leg of multiple expansion toward the bull-case scenario. Until then, the valuation offered a reasonable margin of safety against execution missteps while retaining meaningful upside optionality to the advanced-node acceleration that Entegris's product portfolio was uniquely positioned to capture.

chapters.title: Quarterly Cadence: From CMC Integration Headwinds to Advanced-Node Recovery
chapters.body:
The ten quarterly reporting cycles from Q4 2023 through Q1 2026 constitute the most consequential financial chapter in Entegris's post-CMC Materials life. They encompass the completion of a portfolio rationalization program, the navigation of a semiconductor industry cyclical correction, and — most recently — the first signs of an advanced-node demand supercycle beginning to express itself in the revenue line. The arc is neither linear nor simple: China headwinds interrupted recoveries, CMP pricing concessions compressed margins even as volumes grew, and leadership transitioned mid-cycle. What the record ultimately shows is a business with durable structural advantages and a leverage burden it is repaying on the trajectory management originally committed to.

## Summary Scorecard

The table below covers the period from Q4 2023 through Q1 2026. Quarterly revenue and non-GAAP EPS figures for Q4 2023 through Q3 2025 are approximated from annual totals reported in the [Entegris 10-K 2024](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm); Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin and all Q1 2026 metrics reflect figures as reported in the [Q4 2025 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000009/entgq42025ex991.htm) and [Q1 2026 earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000099/entgq12026ex991.htm).

| Quarter | Net Sales ($M, approx.) | Adj. EBITDA Margin | Non-GAAP Dil. EPS | Primary Management Theme | Guidance vs. Result |
|---------|------------------------|--------------------|--------------------|--------------------------|---------------------|
| Q4 2023 | ~$780 | ~28% | ~$0.72 | Segment reorg; EC divestiture proceeds to debt | In-line |
| Q1 2024 | ~$740 | ~27.5% | ~$0.68 | Cyclical trough; PIM divestiture close (March) | Slight revenue miss |
| Q2 2024 | ~$800 | ~28.5% | ~$0.74 | Sequential recovery; TSMC N3 pull strengthens | Beat |
| Q3 2024 | ~$855 | ~29% | ~$0.82 | TSMC N3 ramp; HBM3 volumes; strongest period | Beat |
| Q4 2024 | ~$846 | ~27.5% | ~$0.74 | Seasonal softness; $625M FY2024 net debt repaid | In-line |
| Q1 2025 | ~$773 | ~27% | ~$0.70 | China headwinds; memory inventory correction | Miss vs. midpoint |
| Q2 2025 | ~$800 | ~27.5% | ~$0.74 | Advanced-node recovery; CMP pricing pressure | In-line |
| Q3 2025 | ~$803 | ~27.5% | ~$0.74 | Reeder appointed CEO August 18; Loy to Exec. Chair | In-line |
| Q4 2025 | ~$820 | **27.7%** | ~$0.76 | Reeder's first full quarter; EBITDA beats guidance | Beat on EBITDA |
| Q1 2026 | **$812** | Above guidance midpoint | **$0.86** | 5% YoY growth; EPS beats consensus | Beat |

## 2024: Divestiture Math and the Two-Speed Recovery

The opening quarter of calendar 2024 was the nadir of the post-CMC era. Approximately $740 million in net sales reflected the compounding of two simultaneous forces: the semiconductor industry's inventory correction, which had pushed fab utilization below historical norms and reduced consumables pull across CMP and filtration alike, and the structural repositioning of the revenue perimeter following the Electronic Chemicals exit in October 2023. The PIM divestiture completed on March 1, 2024, removing the final non-semiconductor business and delivering a further $263 million toward a debt stack that remained the company's most consequential financial constraint.

CEO Bertrand Loy's framing through 2024 distinguished consistently between the transitory compression of the integration period and the structural earnings power the combined CMC-Entegris franchise would eventually deliver. His commentary across multiple calls characterized the advanced-node qualification pipeline — particularly the deepening engagement with TSMC's N3 process nodes — as the leading indicator that mattered most for the medium-term revenue trajectory, even as near-term fab utilization recovered slowly.

The second half of 2024 validated that framework. Third-quarter net sales of approximately $855 million represented the strongest period since the acquisition, with TSMC's N3 ramp driving elevated demand for EUV reticle pods and hafnium-based ALD precursors simultaneously, while SK Hynix's HBM3 production intensity — underpinning its AI accelerator supply leadership — pulled through higher-than-anticipated CMP slurry volumes. Adjusted EBITDA margins for the nine months ended September 2024 averaged approximately [28.5%](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1101302/000110130225000015/entg-20241231.htm), the high-water mark of the post-CMC period. Full-year 2024 debt repayment of approximately $625 million — reducing gross long-term debt from $4.67 billion to approximately $4.04 billion — was the most concrete demonstration that the leverage burden, while heavy, was serviceable at the cadence management had communicated.

The guidance revision cycle in 2024 followed a pattern of modest conservatism. The two beat quarters — Q2 and Q3 — were driven primarily by faster-than-expected advanced-node consumables pull, while Q4's in-line result reflected the seasonal softening typical of year-end customer procurement patterns combined with the early signs of the memory inventory overhang that would resurface in Q1 2025.

## 2025: Interrupted Recovery and the CMP Pricing Drag

Calendar 2025 opened with a material disappointment. First-quarter net sales of approximately $773 million — implied by the [5% year-over-year comparison to Q1 2026's $812 million](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000099/entgq12026ex991.htm) — fell short of the guidance midpoint, with two headwinds arriving simultaneously: incremental U.S. export control tightening that compressed China revenue below the prior quarter's level, and a round of memory customer inventory adjustments as HBM production pacing was recalibrated against AI accelerator delivery schedules at hyperscale customers.

China's revenue dynamic deserves particular attention in the revision narrative. Entegris's exposure — concentrated in SMIC, Hua Hong Semiconductor, and related state-backed fabs, representing an estimated 10–15% of consolidated sales — was largely confined to mature-node processes at or above 28 nanometers, historically below the threshold requiring intensive export licensing management. The successive rounds of restriction expansion across 2024 and 2025 broadened the scope in ways that created periodic drag even in legacy product lines. Loy, through his final quarters as CEO, consistently characterized China as a manageable headwind against a backdrop of structural advanced-node growth that more than offset any structural China reduction over a multi-quarter horizon — a framing that the Q2 and Q3 2025 sequential recovery partially vindicated even as the China overhang persisted.

Through the middle quarters of 2025, adjusted EBITDA margins settled into the [27–28% range](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000009/entgq42025ex991.htm) against a revenue base averaging approximately $800 million per quarter. The persistently sub-30% margins reflected a structural tension that had been underappreciated in the original CMC acquisition thesis: while volume growth in advanced-node CMP and ALD precursors was real and sustained, standard CMP slurry pricing remained under pressure as customers who had extracted concessions during the 2022–2023 downturn were slow to renegotiate. The approximately $300 million in incremental debt repayment during 2025 — reducing net leverage from above 4.0× to approximately 3.8× adjusted EBITDA — confirmed that the cash generation engine was functioning, but also that the pace of deleveraging was calibrated tightly against the prevailing free cash flow margin of [12.7% of net sales](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000009/entgq42025ex991.htm).

## Q4 2025: Reeder's Inflection Quarter

The fourth quarter of 2025 was David Reeder's first full quarter at the helm, and its financial result provided the earliest evidence that the leadership transition coincided with a directional shift in operational discipline. [Adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.7%](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000009/entgq42025ex991.htm) exceeded the guidance range, driven by a combination of favorable product mix — EUV reticle pod volumes and advanced ALD precursor attach rates both running above guidance assumptions — and the early effects of the cost-reduction program that Reeder had signaled as a priority upon assuming the role.

Reeder's communications in the Q4 2025 cycle reflected the capital-allocation orientation he had developed across his tenure at GlobalFoundries and Chewy. Where Loy had framed the CMC integration in terms of portfolio breadth and customer co-development partnerships, Reeder's language centered on free cash flow conversion, the return of capital optionality that deleveraging toward the sub-3.0× net leverage target would eventually restore, and the specific operational levers — manufacturing cost per unit, CMP mix shift toward advanced-node formulations, and APS filtration attach-rate expansion at new fab openings — available to close the remaining gap to 30% adjusted EBITDA.

The Q4 2025 EBITDA beat above guidance was, in itself, a modest outperformance. Its strategic significance was disproportionate: it established that Reeder's cost-discipline messaging was translating into financial results within a single quarter of his full tenure, and it set a floor for the performance expectations embedded in full-year 2026 consensus.

## Q1 2026: Validation and the 30% Margin Path

The [Q1 2026 result](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001101302/000110130226000099/entgq12026ex991.htm) delivered on the promise the Q4 2025 beat had implied. Net sales of $812 million — 5% above the prior-year period — marked the return of durable top-line growth after the flat-to-declining revenue arc of 2025. Non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.86 exceeded consensus; adjusted gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin both cleared their respective guidance midpoints.

The quarter's significance for the 2026 consensus trajectory lies in what it implies about the underlying demand drivers. A 5% year-over-year revenue increase in Q1 2026, against a Q1 2025 baseline that was itself depressed by China headwinds and memory inventory correction, suggests that underlying advanced-node consumables demand — filtration, EUV pods, ALD precursors, and advanced CMP formulations — is growing at a rate materially above the top-line headline. The mix shift toward higher-margin advanced-node products, if sustained, is the single variable most capable of bridging the gap between the current 27–28% adjusted EBITDA margin range and the 30% medium-term target.

The path carries risks. Entegris guided Q2 2026 to $815–$845 million in revenue, non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.76–$0.84, and adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 26.5–27.5% — a sequential step-down from Q1's result that reflects anticipated manufacturing investment headwinds and continued CMP pricing pressure. The EPS guidance midpoint of $0.80 below Q1's $0.86 will test whether Q1 2026 represented genuine acceleration or a beneficiary of favorable quarterly phasing. What the eight-quarter record establishes unambiguously is the discipline of the underlying business: five consecutive quarters of in-line or better EBITDA outcomes since Q4 2024, nearly $925 million of aggregate gross debt repaid across 2024 and 2025, and a management team that has consistently delivered on the margin line even when the revenue line disappointed. The 30% target remains a 2027–2028 probability rather than a near-term certainty, but the cadence of progress has not wavered.

chapters.title: David Reeder's Mandate: Capital Discipline, Margin Expansion, and the Purity Platform's Next Phase
chapters.body:
## An Unconventional Choice for an Unconventional Moment

When Entegris's board announced on August 18, 2025, that David Reeder would succeed Bertrand Loy as President and Chief Executive Officer, the semiconductor materials industry took note of what the succession was not. Reeder was not a specialty chemist. He had not spent a career in process materials, slurry formulation, or filtration engineering. His résumé traced instead a deliberately cross-disciplinary arc — chemical engineering undergraduate training at the University of Arkansas, an MBA from Southern Methodist University, and two decades of senior leadership that moved through semiconductor IDMs, systems companies, a foundry, a retail platform, and two industries entirely unrelated to silicon. The board, it was evident, had not searched for a chemicals-sector operator. It had searched for a capital-structure architect.

[Reeder's career](https://www.entegris.com/en/home/about-us/corporate-overview/david-reeder.html) began in the semiconductor industry proper, with stints at Texas Instruments, Broadcom, and Cisco Systems that gave him foundational fluency in the economics and relationships of the chip supply chain. The pivotal chapter came at GlobalFoundries, where he served as Chief Financial Officer and led the company's initial public offering on NASDAQ in October 2021 — at the time the largest IPO in semiconductor industry history, raising approximately $2.6 billion and valuing the foundry at roughly $25 billion. That transaction required Reeder to manage the complexity of taking a sprawling, privately held wafer manufacturer public against a volatile backdrop, coordinating debt refinancing, investor education, and the optics of a company still in the midst of a strategic reorientation away from leading-edge nodes. It was precisely the kind of capital-markets heavy lifting that the Entegris board needed in a chief executive inheriting a balance sheet still carrying the weight of the $6.5 billion CMC Materials acquisition.

Reeder's path between GlobalFoundries and Entegris included two CEO tenures that raised occasional eyebrows among semiconductor analysts: Lexmark International from 2015 to 2017, where he led the printer and imaging company through its acquisition by a Chinese consortium, and Tower Hill Insurance Group from 2017 to 2020. These detours into sectors remote from semiconductor materials were framed by the board not as liabilities but as evidence of operational range — the ability to manage P&Ls, stakeholder relationships, and strategic pivots across different business models. He returned to the semiconductor adjacency at Chewy, where he served as CFO before the board appointed him an Entegris director in March 2024, a 17-month observation period that gave both sides a mutual diligence window before the [CEO succession](https://investor.entegris.com/news/news-details/2025/Entegris-Announces-CEO-Succession-Plan/default.aspx) was formalized.

## The GlobalFoundries Thread: A New CFO and a Shared Operating Philosophy

Within nine months of Reeder's arrival in the chief executive role, Entegris completed a second significant leadership transition. [Sukhi Nagesh was appointed Chief Financial Officer effective May 18, 2026](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260430507806/en/Entegris-Announces-Appointment-of-Sukhi-Nagesh-as-Chief-Financial-Officer), following an interim period. Nagesh brought nearly three decades of semiconductor-adjacent finance, investor relations, and corporate development experience accumulated across a career that spanned GlobalFoundries — where he held the role of Vice President of Corporate Development, Strategy, and Investor Relations — Marvell Technology, Applied Materials, Brooks Automation, Asyst Technologies, and Nielsen Holdings, where he led corporate development and M&A.

The coincidence of both the incoming CEO and CFO holding recent GlobalFoundries credentials was not coincidental. GlobalFoundries is a company defined by manufacturing discipline, cost efficiency at scale, and rigorous capital allocation — attributes that distinguish it from the fabless and IDM segments of the industry. Its operational culture prizes yield improvement, asset utilization, and supply-chain precision in an environment where margins are structurally thinner than in fabless design or equipment supply. Importing that philosophy into a specialty materials company that had historically priced on value and customer intimacy rather than volume efficiency represented a deliberate inflection. For a company carrying approximately $3.7 billion in gross debt as of late 2025, the operational and financial disciplines associated with the GlobalFoundries background were arguably more valuable than deep familiarity with slurry chemistry.

## Bertrand Loy's Fourteen Years: Architect of the Platform, Author of the Leverage

To understand the mandate Reeder inherited, it is necessary to reckon with the scope of what Bertrand Loy built across his approximately 14-year tenure as President and CEO — and the strategic choices that defined it.

Loy assumed the top role at a company that, in the early 2010s, was generating roughly $400 million in annual revenue, principally from polymer wafer carriers, filtration cartridges, and fluid-handling components — vital products within the semiconductor ecosystem but not the kind of technology-differentiated platform that commanded premium multiples or attracted the breadth of customer co-development relationships that underpin durable competitive advantage. His first landmark transaction was the 2014 acquisition of ATMI Inc. for approximately $1.15 billion, a deal that transformed Entegris's addressable market overnight. ATMI brought atomic-layer deposition and chemical vapor deposition precursors, specialty gas purification, and ion implantation materials into the portfolio, positioning Entegris for the first time as a credible supplier across multiple points in the process flow rather than solely at the containment and filtration layers.

The ATMI integration was executed without significant controversy, and by the late 2010s Entegris was generating revenue well above $1 billion, with an increasingly differentiated portfolio and deepening relationships with TSMC, Samsung, and Intel process development teams. The company's co-engineering model — qualifying specific formulations or filtration membranes into chipmaker process flows in ways that made substitution technically hazardous — was yielding the customer retention characteristics that justify specialty-materials valuations.

The CMC Materials acquisition, announced in December 2021 and completed in July 2022 for approximately $6.5 billion in enterprise value, was a different order of magnitude — and a different order of controversy. Funding the transaction primarily with debt loaded Entegris's balance sheet in a manner that absorbed the company's free cash flow capacity for years and left it exposed to any sustained downturn in wafer starts. Critics at announcement pointed to the leverage as imprudent for a company whose revenue base, while sticky, remained subject to semiconductor-cycle amplitude. CMC's CMP slurries and polishing pads were attractive assets — they served the planarization steps whose frequency increases with node advancement — but the purchase price implied a full strategic premium, and the antitrust clearance process with China's SAMR added months of execution uncertainty.

In retrospect, the 2023–2024 portfolio rationalization program — the divestiture of the Electronic Chemicals business to FUJIFILM for gross proceeds of $675.3 million in October 2023, and the sale of the Pipeline and Infrastructure Materials business to SCF Partners for $263.2 million in March 2024 — represented Loy and the board's pragmatic response to the leverage burden: shed lower-differentiation revenue lines, direct proceeds to debt repayment, and sharpen the remaining portfolio around the advanced-node consumables categories that carry the highest value-per-wafer intensity. Both divestitures reduced reported revenue, but they also improved the quality of the remaining earnings stream and accelerated the deleveraging trajectory.

Whether the CMC deal will ultimately be judged as value-creating depends heavily on the 2026–2028 period. The five-year post-close horizon is the interval over which the combined entity's enhanced cross-selling surface, CMP market leadership, and advanced-node positioning should generate sufficient incremental EBITDA to justify the acquisition premium over a standalone Entegris trajectory.
