financials.key_finding:
Entegris entered fiscal 2025 carrying approximately $4.0 billion in gross long-term debt — the principal legacy of the July 2022 acquisition of CMC Materials — and delivered a year of operational discipline that brought net leverage from above 4.0× to approximately 3.8× adjusted EBITDA by year-end. Full-year 2025 net revenue was approximately $3.2 billion, essentially flat with 2024's post-divestiture base of $3,241 million, but unit-driven volume growth of approximately 2% reflected the ongoing ramp of advanced-node wafer starts at leading-edge foundry and memory customers. Adjusted EBITDA margins hovered in the 27–28% range through 2025, below the company's medium-term target of approximately 30%, as CMP pricing pressure and the dilutive effect of reshoring-related manufacturing investments weighed on profitability. Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin of 27.7% came in above guidance, and full-year 2025 free cash flow margin reached 12.7% of net sales — approximately $405–410 million — enabling roughly $300 million of incremental debt repayment during the year.

For Q1 2026, Entegris reported net sales of $812 million — a 5% year-over-year improvement — with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.86 exceeding consensus; adjusted gross margin and adjusted EBITDA margin both exceeded guidance. Management guided Q2 2026 revenue to $815–$845 million, non-GAAP diluted EPS of $0.76–$0.84, and adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 26.5–27.5%.

Capital structure remains the most consequential near-term variable. Total assets at December 31, 2024 were $8.39 billion, anchored by $3.94 billion in goodwill from the CMC acquisition and $1.09 billion in net intangible assets, leaving tangible book value deeply negative. Gross long-term debt was approximately $4.04 billion at fiscal year-end 2024, reduced from $4.67 billion at year-end 2023 through approximately $625 million of net repayments. R&D (engineering, research and development) expenses were approximately $315 million for fiscal 2024, representing approximately 9.7% of net revenue — above the specialty-chemicals sector average and reflecting the co-development partnership model with leading-edge customers. GAAP net income for 2024 was $292.8 million ($1.93 diluted EPS), substantially suppressed by annual amortization of acquisition-related intangibles of approximately $200 million and net interest expense exceeding $250 million.
structural_observations: Revenue base: FY2024 net revenue of $3,241 million and FY2025 approximately $3,196 million reflect a post-divestiture perimeter following the removal of the Electronic Chemicals ($675 million proceeds, October 2023) and PIM ($263 million proceeds, March 2024) businesses; organic unit-driven revenue growth of approximately 2% in 2025 tracked industry wafer-start growth, led by CMP consumables, liquid filtration, and selective etch chemistries.

Fiscal year cadence: Calendar fiscal year ending December 31; the company reports on a 52/53-week basis with quarters ending in late March, late June, late September, and late December or early January; Q1 2026 ended March 28, 2026.

Margin progression: Adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 28.5% for the nine months ended September 2024, remained in the 27–28% range through 2025 quarters (Q4 2025: 27.7%), and compares to a stated medium-term management target of approximately 30%; reaching the target requires a combination of advanced-node revenue scale recovery and operational leverage from the post-CMC integration cost program.

Capital structure: Gross long-term debt of approximately $4.04 billion at December 31, 2024 (down from $4.67 billion at December 31, 2023), consisting primarily of senior secured term loans and senior unsecured notes; net leverage reduced to approximately 3.8× adjusted EBITDA by year-end 2025; management's stated medium-term target is below 3.0× net leverage.

Debt vs. equity: Total assets of $8.39 billion are dominated by goodwill ($3.94 billion) and net intangibles ($1.09 billion) from the CMC acquisition, with net property, plant, and equipment of $1.62 billion; approximately 151 million diluted shares outstanding at December 31, 2024; GAAP stockholders' equity is compressed by the debt load and acquisition amortization, making non-GAAP metrics the operative performance lens.

Comparable peers: Direct public-company comparables include Merck KGaA (Electronics/Performance Materials segment), Pall Corporation (Danaher), and Air Products and Chemicals (specialty gases); semiconductor materials sector EV/EBITDA multiples in the 2025–2026 period ranged approximately 15–28× for advanced-node-exposed names; Entegris in May 2026 traded at approximately 20–27× forward adjusted EBITDA at an estimated market capitalization of $20–22 billion.

Market cap volatility: ENTG shares have exhibited significant cyclical volatility — trading above $160 in 2021 during peak semiconductor capital expenditure sentiment, falling below $70 in mid-2023 amid CMC integration concerns, sector correction, and leverage anxiety, and recovering to approximately $130–140 in May 2026 as advanced-node volume recovery and deleveraging progress restored investor confidence.

leadership.key_finding:
Entegris is in the first stage of a dual leadership transition of meaningful strategic significance. Bertrand Loy, who served as President and CEO for approximately 14 years and was the architect of the company's multi-divisional portfolio strategy and the $6.5 billion CMC Materials acquisition, transitioned to Executive Chair in August 2025, handing the president-and-CEO title to David Reeder. This succession represents the company's first CEO change since approximately 2012 and brings to the helm an executive with a deliberately different background: Reeder is a chemical engineer (B.S., University of Arkansas) with an MBA from Southern Methodist University whose career combines deep semiconductor-industry relationships forged at Texas Instruments, Broadcom, Cisco, and GlobalFoundries with hands-on capital-structure and IPO experience. At GlobalFoundries, where he served as CFO, Reeder led the company's NASDAQ IPO in 2021 — at the time the largest IPO in semiconductor industry history — and oversaw supply chain and procurement functions. He also held CEO roles at Lexmark International (2015–2017) and Tower Hill Insurance Group (2017–2020) before returning to the semiconductor supply chain at Chewy as CFO and then joining Entegris's board in March 2024.

Concurrently, Entegris appointed Sukhi Nagesh as CFO effective May 18, 2026, following an interim period. Nagesh brings nearly 30 years of semiconductor-adjacent finance, investor relations, and M&A experience from GlobalFoundries, Marvell Technology, Applied Materials, Brooks Automation, Asyst Technologies, and Nielsen. The twin appointments of Reeder and Nagesh — both with recent GlobalFoundries connections — may signal a management philosophy oriented toward manufacturing operational discipline and capital-efficiency rigor.

The board is chaired by Bertrand Loy in his Executive Chair capacity. The full board composition, director biographies, committee assignments, and executive compensation structure are detailed in the April 2026 definitive proxy statement (DEF 14A) filed with the SEC.
research_notes_for_writer: Dig into Reeder's specific mandate from the board: the succession announcement language emphasized capital discipline and deleveraging, but probe whether the board also gave Reeder a latent M&A mandate to pursue once leverage reaches a target corridor, and whether that distinction influences his public messaging on capital allocation.

Examine Bertrand Loy's 14-year legacy in full: Loy grew Entegris from a roughly $400 million revenue company to a $3.2 billion one and executed the ATMI and CMC acquisitions; the CMC deal was controversial at announcement given the leverage load; a balanced assessment of whether CMC will prove value-creating over the 5-year post-close horizon is essential to understanding the board's succession rationale.

Analyze the GlobalFoundries overlap between Reeder and Nagesh: both have GFS background, and this is not coincidental; explore whether this shared operational philosophy — GFS is known for discipline in high-volume, cost-sensitive fab operations — is being imported into a specialty materials company that has historically priced on value rather than volume.

Review the April 2026 proxy statement (DEF 14A) carefully for compensation design: the alignment of short-term incentive metrics (revenue growth? EBITDA margin? leverage reduction?) reveals the board's actual near-term priorities and whether they are tilted toward deleveraging or revenue growth.

Probe the board's independent director composition and committee assignments beyond the Loy/Reeder relationship: identify directors with private equity, activist investor, or semiconductor-customer relationships that may have influenced the succession timing and the portfolio rationalization decisions of 2023–2024.

Investigate Reeder's non-semiconductor CEO tenures at Lexmark and Tower Hill Insurance Group — sectors unrelated to semiconductor materials — to assess how the board resolved concerns about industry-specific credibility and how sell-side analysts and institutional investors received his appointment in August 2025.

Research any retention or employment agreements for legacy CMC Materials executives who joined the combined company post-acquisition: the degree to which the CMC-originated talent base has been integrated, retained, or departed is material to understanding the integration execution risk and the management bench depth available to Reeder and Nagesh.
